findings.summary: Slack identity revocation is not wired to the lifecycle producers required by the task.
findings.details: S10-T01 requires organization-scoped Slack identity bindings to revoke when a user requests unlinking, when organization membership or the user is suspended, and when the Slack connection is replaced. The implementation adds an internal revokeSlackIdentityLinksForLifecycle mutation and blocks pending activation by rechecking the owner, but no task-owned membership, user, or provider-connection lifecycle path invokes that mutation. Connection replacement revocation is also opportunistic: active rows for a stale generation are revoked only if a later pending Slack confirmation happens to observe the stale connection. Active bindings can therefore remain durable after the required lifecycle producers fire, leaving a stale exact Slack identity binding until some unrelated path manually revokes or encounters it.
